correctness.rationale: Under the stated Steiner normalization the generator-wedge sum gives V_3. By Cauchy–Binet, each forest component contributes its vertex count to the Gram determinant, since every maximal incidence minor obtained by deleting a row has determinant ±1. The only triple determinants are 4,6,8. Counting disjoint edge-pairs inside triples gives (m−2)M_2=P_4+2b+3M_3, where b counts triples with two components. Any nonstar has a three-edge path; taking its end edges and an edge outside that path gives a disconnected triple and hence strict star minimality. Leaf deletion bounds the three-matching count by the path value, and the strict path advantage in D=(m−2)M_2−P_4 is (m−2)(Σ_v binom(deg(v)−1,2)−1)+P_4(T)>0 for nonpaths (separate star case). The positive coefficients, path run counts, gap, ratio and two spider counts all check. `python3 /workspace/reviews/evidence/reproduce.py 4` independently enumerated 1,296 and 16,807 labeled trees of orders 6 and 7 by Prüfer codes, checked the determinant counts and detected exactly the labeled stars and paths at equality. This finite replay supplements the proof; the supplied checker was read, not run.
